svg.aria-label: Diagram: an AWS Config compliance view showing nothing non-compliant can mean four different things. The configuration recorder decides what exists to evaluate and by default records all supported resources in the Region where AWS Config is running, so a resource in a Region with no recorder produces no configuration item and nothing to evaluate. A service-linked configuration recorder has its scope set by the linked service rather than by the customer. Rules return four evaluation results: NON_COMPLIANT means the rule fails the compliance check, ERROR means a parameter is invalid or malformed, and NOT_APPLICABLE filters out resources the rule's logic cannot apply to. Only one of those is a failure and two of them look like success. Charging is per configuration item recorded, per rule evaluation and per conformance pack evaluation, priced per rule evaluation per region, while consolidated billing measures the total evaluations from all accounts.
svg.title: Two filters sit above the dashboard, and both of them produce green
svg.text: Between a resource and a finding, two things can quietly say nothing.
AWS Config — what the recorder captured, and whether the rule managed to evaluate it.
FILTER 1 — the recorder, per Region
“By default … records all supported resources in
the AWS Region where AWS Config is running”
No recorder → no configuration item → nothing to
evaluate, and no trace in Config at all.
Narrowing scope looks exactly like deleting a rule.
FILTER 2 — did the rule actually run
NON_COMPLIANT “fails the conditions” a failure
ERROR “not valid … or is broken
formatted incorrectly”
NOT_APPLICABLE “logic … cannot be correct,
applied to” still not a check
What “nothing non-compliant” can actually mean
1 the rule evaluated the resource and it passed → a check
2 NOT_APPLICABLE — the rule does not apply here → not a check, correctly
3 ERROR — the rule’s own parameters are malformed → not a check, and broken
4 never recorded — no configuration item exists → the rule never saw it
A conformance pack is an authored file
“a collection of AWS Config rules and remediation
actions … deployed as a single entity”
Authored as a YAML template; can be stored as an
SSM document and deployed by name.
The remediation half is the part people skim.
Per-Region decision, organisation-wide tier
priced “per rule evaluation per region”
“With consolidated billing, AWS will measure the
total … from all of your accounts”
One team’s enthusiastic pack moves everybody’s
position on the curve, and nobody owns that number.
The audit: rules in ERROR, and rules evaluating entirely as NOT_APPLICABLE
Both occupy a tile, both are counted among your controls, and neither is checking anything. The first is a defect;
the second is usually a sample pack deployed where it does not fit — and you pay per evaluation for both.
Then list the Regions with no recorder.
Resources there are neither compliant nor non-compliant. They are absent, and absence is the one state no Config
view will show you.
AWS publishes every one of these states and bills in a way that makes the waste visible. It just does not put them
on the tile, and the tile is what gets screenshotted into the compliance report.
